OS: Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS, bash 5.2
captured: 2026-09-06T12:45:00Z
file: ~/.bash_history  (-rw------- 41991 bytes, 2000 lines)

Real lines off a real server, rearranged into a short run and with nothing
personal in them — the project names here are infrastructure ones that came
with the tools. What was kept is every shape that breaks a naive parser:

- **No timestamps at all.** HISTTIMEFORMAT was not set, which is the Ubuntu
  default, so the file has zero `#<epoch>` lines. The history has an order and
  no times. A screen that says "3 months ago" over this is inventing.
- **A multi-line command is stored as separate lines.** `sh -c '` opens a quote
  and the next four lines finish it. Read line by line, one command becomes
  five, four of which are not commands.
- **Pasted output gets in.** Two lines here are log output from a previous
  command that somebody pasted at a prompt. Nothing distinguishes them from a
  command, and nothing should pretend to.
- **`cd $PROJECT_DIR`** cannot be resolved from the text. Neither can `cd -`.
- Relative moves (`cd ..`, `cd ../test-logs/`) and absolute ones are mixed.

Not represented, because this server had none: a zsh history with
EXTENDED_HISTORY (`: <epoch>:<dur>;<cmd>`), and a bash file where
HISTTIMEFORMAT was set.
